import numpy as np, json, os, re
def load():

    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))

import numpy as np, os, re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
# Determine, per demo, WHICH transform+window of the many matches corresponds to center-axis reflection geometry, then infer test answer.
# Geometric model: source window W (r0,r1,c0,c1) relates to hole via central inversion through grid midpoint? For a h*w hole at rows hh..hv, cols hw..hw1:
#   under V-mirror across horizontal midline: source cell for hole cell (r,c) is (R-1-r, c) -> source region rows (R-1-hv)-(R-1-hh) ... source window rows = R-1-hv .. R-1-hh (reversed). So expected win r0=R-1-hv, c0=hw, tn=flipud. Under H-mirror: win rows hh..hv, cols C-1-hw1..C-1-hw, tn=fliplr.
for k in [1,2,3,4]:
    X=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {k} input']); O=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {k} output'])
    R,C=X.shape; h,w=O.shape
    pos=[(int(r),int(c)) for r,c in np.argwhere(X==8)]
    hh=min(p[0] for p in pos); hv=max(p[0] for p in pos); hw=min(p[1] for p in pos); hwm=max(p[1] for p in pos)
    # predicted windows
    pred={'V_flipud':(R-1-hv,hw),'H_fliplr':(hh,C-1-hwm)}
    for name,(r0,c0) in pred.items():
        S=X[r0:r0+h,c0:c0+w]
        tn=('flipud' if name=='V_flipud' else 'fliplr')
        good = np.array_equal(np.flipud(S),O) if name=='V_flipud' else np.array_equal(np.fliplr(S),O)
        print('demo',k,name,(r0,c0),'match:',good, 'S==O without flip:',np.array_equal(S,O))
